deep.reconstruction: Almost nothing on this page can be reconstructed. The visible writing is mirror-reversed bleed-through from the other side of the leaf. The only non-reversed mark is the archival folio number '13' at the top right. The ghost text sits in the right half of the sheet and has the same layout as the transcription supplied as the 'next page': a block of about 7 lines of prose, a short heading, about 3 lines, a section number '11.' (in the next-page transcription it appears as 'II.'), and about 10 lines of prose with inline formula fragments. One fragment looks like a vanishing condition of the form '... = 0' with a bracketed group of derivatives. Then come two more prose paragraphs and a four-line case table, consistent with the next-page transcription: 'für p = 1 ..., ϑ(...) = 0, r = 0'; 'p = ..., ϑ(...) = 0, r = 0'; 'p = 2, 3 ..., ϑ(...) = 0, r = ...(p−1)'; 'p ≥ ... , ϑ(...) = 0, r = ...(p−1)'. This page therefore carries no independent content. It is the reverse of the leaf whose text was transcribed as the next page. That text appears to discuss, case by case in the genus p, where a theta function vanishes and the number r of something depending on p. This is plausibly the circle of ideas around the zeros of the Riemann theta function (cf. the 1857 Abelian functions paper and the 1865 theta-vanishing paper), but my reading is speculative. No derivation can be restated with any certainty, and I add no steps of my own.

results.what: Case distinction by genus p for the vanishing of ϑ(...) and an associated integer r (=0 for small p, something like a multiple of (p−1) for larger p). This is only seen as show-through, so its content is unverified.
results.modern_name: Possibly related to the Riemann vanishing theorem / theta divisor considerations (speculative)

deep.surprise_reason: The page has no legible original content of its own. It shows the reversed ghost of the other side of the leaf. The faint fragments that can be guessed at (theta vanishing by genus) belong to themes already well known as Riemann's.
transcription_corrections: The page should be described as mirror-reversed show-through of the verso/recto (the leaf transcribed as the 'next page'), not as original text; only the folio number '13' at the top right is written on this side.
The section number read as '11.' corresponds to 'II.' in the next-page transcription; given the mirror image either reading is possible, and 'II.' or '11.' cannot be decided from the ghost.

The bottom four formula lines visible in reverse match the case table 'für p = 1 ... r = 0 / ... / p = 2,3 ... r = ...(p−1) / p ≥ ...' of the next page, confirming that the two images are the two sides of the same sheet.
